verdict.line: You out-range and out-trade him through the laning phase, but if he survives to stack Siphoning Strike and hit level 6 clean, the 49.8% head-to-head over 1629 games turns into a coinflip.

brief.thesis: Nasus's only early trading tool, Q (Siphoning Strike), is a 255-range melee strike on an 8-to-4s cooldown, while your Q (Volcanic Rupture) hits at 800 range with a slow attached — he physically cannot contest you without walking into poke range. That range gap is why lane and solo-kill advantage both sit with you despite the near-even overall win rate; Nasus is built to farm passively here, not duel.

theirWindow.when: You whiff Searing Charge without hitting terrain
theirWindow.what: E (Searing Charge) only knocks up if you collide with terrain while charging; if you miss that and just pass through him, you're stuck in recovery with no shockwave, and Wither (W) decelerating your Move and Attack Speed lets him kite the rest of the trade for free.

yourWindow.when: Nasus steps into melee range to last-hit
yourWindow.what: He has to close to 255 range to secure every cannon or low-health caster minion with Q. Land your Q (Volcanic Rupture) at 800 range as he commits to that last hit — the slow lets you follow with autos before Wither or Spirit Fire can answer.

start.why: Nasus's damage is all physical autos and Siphoning Strike pokes; the flat damage reduction on autos plus the regen lets you hold the poke range advantage without burning potions.

boots.why: Reduces incoming auto-attack damage, which is exactly what both his Siphoning Strike and his Soul Eater-fueled autos deal.

core.why: Highest-winrate path into this matchup (60.3% over 78 games); the burn punishes him for standing in melee to farm.
Returns damage on his autos and cuts his Soul Eater lifesteal, directly countering his late-game sustain race.
Stacks with Living Forge's bonus resistances from all sources, scaling your tankiness past his flat-damage Q stacks.

he's stacked enough Q and lifesteal that his sustained damage output threatens to outheal your trades late

runes.keystoneWhy: Triggers off autos as you poke with Q and follow up, converting to permanent health gain that races Nasus's Soul Eater lifesteal rather than losing to it over time.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite carries the highest measured winrate for this matchup (54.4% over the pick pool) and lines up with your solo-kill advantage — Ignite's burn finishes early punishes before Nasus can stack Soul Eater sustain.

playing.title: Poke every last-hit he takes
playing.detail: His Q (Siphoning Strike) forces him to 255 range to secure kills; your Q (Volcanic Rupture) reaches 800. Hit him on CS and walk away before Wither comes online.

playing.title: Only commit E with a wall behind him
playing.detail: Searing Charge only knocks up on terrain collision. Without a wall to aim at, you're better off not throwing it — a whiffed charge into his Wither is how you lose the trade.

playing.title: Step off Spirit Fire zones
playing.detail: His E (12s cooldown) drops an armor-reducing zone on the ground. Don't stand in it during extended trades, since it directly undercuts your resistance stacking.

playing.title: Respect his level 6 spike
playing.detail: Fury of the Sands gives him bonus health, range, and a max-health drain while active. Don't extend a trade into his ultimate window unless your own Call of the Forge God (R) is also up.

playing.title: Hold W for a Brittle setup, not a poke
playing.detail: Bellows Breath applies Brittle on the final gout, but it's on a 12-to-10s cooldown — save it to combo into E's knockup or R's elemental for a real punish, not a chip trade.

playing.title: Build Thornmail to beat his sustain race
playing.detail: Thornmail's damage return plus the included grievous wounds effect directly cuts into Soul Eater lifesteal, which is his only way back into fights he's behind in.

playing.title: Use Living Forge to snowball the team
playing.detail: Once you're ahead off the range advantage, spend gold on masterwork items for allies from anywhere on the map — convert your early lane lead into a wider team advantage.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample-size numbers above are pulled from measured OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1); the tactical reasoning connecting them to ability ranges and cooldowns is my own read of the matchup.

stats.opponentTip: Nasus will focus early game on farming with (Q) rather than on contesting lane, so prevent him from farming with ease. Be careful of using [E] recklessly as he can use (W) to prevent you from retreating.
